needed_action: Keep all diagnostics separately typed as saved. needed_action: Inspect/re-fit the published phase-resolved circular-polarization spectra using the competing harmonic identifications and clarify whether the changes reflect state/geometry or a prior model assumption. parameter: System taxonomy and Roche-lobe transfer state
competing_evidence: Reimers+99 and Schwarz+01 describe a low-accretion polar/LARP. needed_action: Choose a catalog taxonomy that keeps confirmed magnetic polar/LARP identity separate from proposed detached/pre-polar evolution (recommended dual labels); confirm that no later donor/Roche geometry measurement supersedes Vogel+07.

competing_evidence: Vogel+07 Eq. 1 fits 1999–2005 photometric maxima and RV phase, P_orb=0.11592364(43) d. Reimers+99 preliminary 0.11638 d used just over one cycle. parameter: Orbital-period comparison and possible period evolution
competing_evidence: Greiner+98 Eq. 2: 0.08328388(8) d = 119.928787 min; Hernández-Díaz+25 CDS Table A.1: TESS sectors 52/53 final Fourier period 119.94464±0.00093 min (four method values span 119.9000–119.9800 min; CorrFlag=1). If a single high-precision modern ephemeris or Pdot is needed, obtain phase-resolved follow-up timing and test the TESS detection at its reported faint-source reliability; do not infer asynchronous spin from the period difference.

parameter: 15A X-band radio flux and short-timescale variability
competing_evidence: Barrett+17 printed Table 3 gives 165±25 μJy for 15A-25A (2015-03-09 UTC 08:16:36; 291 s; RCP-only). Until then retain the printed original, CDS-served row, later Barrett+20 Stokes values, and next-day limit as distinct records.

parameter: Cyclotron harmonic assignment and magnetic-field region
competing_evidence: Greiner+98 optical humps near 4500/5700 Å give 50±4 MG for 3rd/4th harmonics under kT=20 keV, viewing angle ~70 deg, log Lambda=3.5; assigning the humps to 2nd/3rd harmonics gives ~70 MG. needed_action: Keep both MG cyclotron alternatives, the kG radio-plasma estimate, and the absence of a photospheric Zeeman measurement distinct. Near-IR/phase-resolved cyclotron spectroscopy would be needed to resolve the harmonic assignment; no immediate catalog choice is warranted.

parameter: 170.59 d long-term photometric modulation / third-body interpretation
competing_evidence: Yang+17 Table 2 reports a 170.59±0.12 d PTF/CRTS photometric modulation (0.90 mag amplitude). No tertiary detection is reported.
why_it_matters: The period is not orbital/spin/radio recurrence, and assigning a tertiary would add an unconfirmed system component that could distort evolutionary interpretations.
needed_action: Retain it as a long-term photometric modulation and label the third-body scenario a model hypothesis only. Independent orbital/tertiary evidence would be required before changing source classification.

competing_evidence: Greiner+98 infer M2=0.16 M_sun, R2=0.2 R_sun and M4–M4.5 from Porb with a main-sequence mass-radius relation; no donor features are detected. competing_evidence: The official publisher-hosted PDF text extraction contains the V1007 Her subsection (WISE W1 noisy/suggestive of ellipsoidal variation; W2 weak single maximum; colors indicate cyclotron contribution), but direct local PDF download failed and no page image was available in this run. competing_evidence: Gänsicke+05 optical spin 1520.510±0.066 s; Anzolin+08 X-ray spin 1528±6 s; Bruch+25 TESS LC1/2/3/5 cluster near 1520.37–.39 s, LC4=1520.494±.014 s flagged outlier. competing_evidence: Barrett+20 Table 2 gives 3210±365 G assuming donor-coronal fundamental ECM (ν≈2.8B MHz); location is not uniquely resolved and this is not WD surface B. parameter: derived diagnostics tied to orbital alias
competing_evidence: Anzolin+08 spin/orbit ratio≈0.096 and M3±1 donor prediction use 4.402 h. TESS sources favor ≈4.846 h, changing both; no component measurements independently settle the choice.

competing_evidence: Pala+22 reanalyzes the Gänsicke+06 HST UV data with Gaia EDR3 and reports 0.63 (+0.10/-0.08) Msun, R=0.013 (+0.0017/-0.0014) Rsun, and 19,248 (+486/-450) K; the original fit using Thorstensen d=79 (+8/-6) pc reported 0.78 (+0.12/-0.17) Msun, 7.61 (+1.6/-1.0)e8 cm, and 19,800 +/-700 K. needed_action: Keep both fit branches in source comparisons; verify whether the intended community-facing default should be the Gaia-rescaled Pala+22 solution, and preserve the non-dynamical/model label.

competing_evidence: Young+81 directly identifies 13 MG Zeeman absorption from an accreting polar-cap region; Wickramasinghe & Martin+85 find a poor-viewing-geometry centered-dipole fit near 22 MG and a better offset-dipole active pole near 14 MG; Bailey+91 IR cyclotron fit gives 14.5 +/-0.3 MG; Campbell+08 low-state IR cyclotron model gives 13.6 (+1.0/-0.8) MG with non-1sigma fit ranges.
why_it_matters: Treating a polar-cap Zeeman value, global field geometry and cyclotron-column fields as one WD surface field would bias population comparisons.
needed_action: Keep the distinct measurements and models separate; if a single field summary is required, choose which component and field geometry it represents. Do not average these values.

parameter: Donor mass ratio and binary inclination
competing_evidence: Southwell+95 reports irradiation-affected K2=198 +/-3 km/s, v sin i=92 +/-9 km/s, and uncorrected q=M2/M1=0.47 +/-0.08 as a lower estimate; corrected solutions are not unique. needed_action: Verify the original Southwell correction and Mason+24 Table 1/Table 2/prose donor-value inconsistency before adopting a unique donor mass or a q-based component mass. Retain the inclination methods separately.

parameter: X-ray flux band, absorption convention, epoch and state
competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 3 quotes 1.1 +/-0.1e-10 erg cm-2 s-1 in 1-10 keV from 4XMM-DR11-derived catalog bands and applies a 10% error floor. needed_action: Query the exact 4XMM-DR11 detection(s) within the published source region; inspect native 0.2-12 keV Flux8, observation date, variability flags and any AM Her source-specific spectral fit. Do not label Ridder's converted value unabsorbed meanwhile.

competing_evidence: Young+81 classifies the visible low-state donor spectrum as M4.5 V; Bailey+91 fits a 3250-K M-dwarf atmosphere template; Mason+24 repeats T2=3290 +/-70 K from Gänsicke+01. needed_action: Retrieve and inspect the cited Gänsicke+01 donor analysis if a direct donor temperature is needed; otherwise preserve all values as spectral/template or secondary-reported estimates.

competing_evidence: RXTE shock model Rana+05: 1.21±0.10 Msun; eclipse geometry Mukai+03: <0.67 Msun; NuSTAR Shaw+20: 0.76(+0.09/−0.08); Swift+NuSTAR Wang+21: 0.85±0.07; Wang Table 4 also reports Ramsay (2000) 0.98 with 90% interval 0.78–1.19. These methods/models are not interchangeable.

needed_action: Keep all results with methods and confidence conventions. If a single community-facing preferred value is required, choose only after checking the original Ramsay article and resolving model systematics; do not average.

parameter: WD effective temperature / HST UV component
competing_evidence: Schmidt & Stockman+01 fit a ~35,000 K blackbody or 25,000–30,000 K atmosphere to dereddened UV-optical flux; their variable eclipse spectra also support stream/other emission, and later Mukai+03 finds a donor-caused X-ray eclipse. Rana+05 kTbb=88±2 eV and Wang+21 ~50 eV are soft X-ray accretion components, not photospheric temperatures.

needed_action: Keep the HST blackbody and atmosphere branches as candidate hot-component fits. Decide whether a white-dwarf photospheric Teff is publishable only after reviewing the original HST component decomposition and extinction assumptions.

competing_evidence: Rana+05 tentatively infers 28–35 MG by assigning a circular-polarization peak to the 6th–8th cyclotron harmonic; no cyclotron spectrum and poor optical polarization data. Ferrario+15 lists ~30 MG as a secondary compilation. Barrett+20 gives 3563±730 G only under fundamental ECM from a donor corona.
why_it_matters: A kG radio-plasma field and an MG accretion-region/WD field are different physical quantities; mixing them would corrupt WD-field comparisons.
needed_action: Keep the 28–35 MG value explicitly tentative and region-specific, keep 3.56 kG as conditional donor-corona radio field, and do not quote a secure global WD surface field without direct cyclotron/Zeeman evidence.

competing_evidence: Boyd+14 reports quadratic eclipse ephemeris dPorb/dt/P=−1.38(29)×10^-11 yr yr^-1 using a 15-year, multi-source timing compilation. Littlefield+15 finds no evidence for derivative in its 28-month eclipse set but explicitly says the result does not contradict Boyd’s longer dataset.
why_it_matters: A changing orbital period affects long-term timing and could be confused with the WD spin derivative or beat evolution.
needed_action: For any adopted orbital Pdot, harmonize eclipse-time datasets, time standards and error reweighting; otherwise retain the long-baseline claim and the shorter-baseline nondetection separately.

competing_evidence: Staubert+03 combined and optical-only fits give different Pdot_spin values; Mukai+03 and Boyd+14 use different baselines/models; Littlefield+15 cubic polynomial and exponential spin ephemerides both fit. needed_action: Keep fit-specific ephemerides, epochs and models in the measurement table. Do not select one extrapolation as a measured current period without a common timing refit.

competing_evidence: Rana+05 Table 4 reports 1–10 keV average 2.13×10^-11 and says fluxes correct local absorbers only while setting interstellar NH=0; nearby prose calls hard flux unabsorbed. why_it_matters: An ambiguous absorption correction or noncontemporaneous catalog flux can bias radio/X-ray luminosity and accretion-state comparisons.
needed_action: Inspect the exact Rana Table 4 note/model and match Ridder’s V1432 row to its 4XMM detection/model/NH. Until then retain separate flux rows without calling either Ridder value unabsorbed.

parameter: radio detection significance and emission site
competing_evidence: Barrett+20 lists a detection with custom S/N=9.3, but Table 1 Stokes I=15±5 μJy (~3σ) and CP=+100±47% (~2.1σ). The source is unresolved; a donor-coronal fundamental ECM origin is proposed, not localized.
why_it_matters: Detection thresholds affect sample membership, and the emission site determines whether the conditional kG field can be compared to WD fields.
needed_action: Preserve Barrett’s published detection plus raw Stokes measurements. For thresholded population work, apply a consistent Stokes-I threshold; do not treat the donor-corona mechanism as confirmed.

competing_evidence: Schmidt & Stockman+01 say an M4 V donor was detected in I band and cite Patterson+95; the original Patterson full text was not retrieved. needed_action: Retrieve/check Patterson+95 original I-band spectrum and retain model masses separately from direct donor quantities; seek dynamical velocities or resolved donor spectrum before adopting q/Teff.

competing_evidence: Boyd+14 presents a pre-record nova as the origin of asynchronism and projects synchronization near 2100. Wang+21 argues the low inferred Mdot contradicts a recent-nova classification under the short synchronization-timescale picture; its rate and timing extrapolation are also model-dependent.
why_it_matters: A speculative post-nova history could be mistaken for an established evolutionary pathway connecting populations.
needed_action: Keep both as hypotheses, label model assumptions, and do not use the proposed nova/resynchronization scenario as an established sequence or catalog classification.

parameter: legacy distance input and dependent luminosities
competing_evidence: Historical ~230 pc distance is quoted by Schmidt & Stockman+01 from Watson+95 and used in older Rana+05 luminosities/accretion-rate estimates; HST discussion adjusts it to ~200 pc for assumed I-band extinction. Current Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric posterior is 449.66 pc. Original Watson distance method/error has not been independently checked.

needed_action: If historical luminosities or the Rana Mdot are quantitatively reused, retrieve Watson+95 and decide whether to recompute explicitly from the newer posterior. Keep old published inputs distinct meanwhile.

competing_evidence: Tovmassian+17 infer ~16 MG only if an ~8000 Å continuum turnover is the 8th cyclotron harmonic; they say it could be 35% lower and B>~20 MG is very unlikely. No Zeeman or individual harmonics were detected; Bernardini+13 only reports an IR excess/cyclotron contribution.

needed_action: Decide whether RAWDOG should expose the conditional ~16 MG estimate and qualitative <~20 MG discussion in separate fields or keep the numeric estimate only in the measurement ledger.

competing_evidence: Bernardini+13 Sect. 3.3/Table 5 gives 0.77 +0.02/-0.03 Msun from a Suleimanov post-shock spectral model; Tovmassian+17 adopts 0.75 Msun as a Doppler-map input. No dynamical WD mass was found.

needed_action: Decide which population tables may include the X-ray model estimate; retain the 0.75 Msun map input as assumed only. Verify whether Bernardini explicitly defines the mass interval confidence level outside Table 5.

competing_evidence: Barrett+20 original VLA Table 1 gives 79±5 μJy; Ridder+23 Table 3 repeats 79±8 μJy with an asterisk because the catalog imposes a minimum 10% error. Same detection, not an independent observation.

competing_evidence: Catalán+99 main text/equation defines q=M2/M1=0.54±0.14, while Table 4 labels q=M1/M2 and prints 0.54±0.08. Schwope+00 uses Q=M1/M2=1.75; Watson+03 reports q=M2/M1=0.63 under its Roche-tomography assumptions.

needed_action: Verify whether Catalán+99 has an erratum or author clarification; until then retain both statements and never use its table q as canonical.

needed_action: Keep measurements by method separate. Check original Cropper polarimetry and Watson+03 text/table interpretation (or author clarification) before choosing a preferred inclination/mass branch.

competing_evidence: Catalán+99 directly classifies donor as M4V from TiO; Mukai & Charles 1986 gives M2–4 template range; queried SIMBAD record says M2 D with no traceable citation.

needed_action: Locate the provenance of SIMBAD M2 D and check whether its source predates the direct M4V spectroscopy; keep M4V as the primary measured classification for now.

competing_evidence: Belle+00 states field strength was not directly measured; quotes assumed typical 20–30 MG and indirect <10–30 MG possibility. Ferrario+15 table lists uncertain Bcyc1=30: MG. No primary cyclotron/Zeeman measurement was confirmed.

competing_evidence: QQ Vul is classified as a polar and is conventionally treated as synchronized, but no independent WD spin period was found in inspected papers. Existing compatibility field had stored Porb as spin.

needed_action: Use the orbital period as measured and leave the independent WD-spin numeric field blank; retain synchronism only as interpretation unless an independent spin measurement is found.

competing_evidence: Cropper (1998) original full text is now retrieved and checked. Sect. 5 gives approximate i≈50 deg and magnetic-pole colatitude beta≈40 deg using simple polarization geometry; not a 40–50 deg interval.

needed_action: Closed for access/provenance: original paper checked and its approximate geometry is recorded. Its result remains a competing method-dependent estimate under QQVUL-002.

needed_action: Keep each model estimate in separate component-specific fields; select a canonical model only if a use case requires it.

competing_evidence: Echevarría+08 derive M1=.63±.05, M2=.37±.04 at i=70±3°, q=M2/M1=.60±.02 under donor Roche-fill/corotation assumptions. needed_action: Inspect Li+16 orbital ephemeris derivation and cycle count; label by validity epoch and do not average.

competing_evidence: Exact Gaia DR3 counterpart is supported by name, Gaia ID, published Tycho-2 position/proper motion and propagated position, but Gaia RUWE=1.7625, astrometric_excess_noise=0.2507 mas with significance=91.0, phot_variable_flag=VARIABLE, BP/RP flux-over-error 6.99/11.82 and BP/RP excess factor=1.5252.

parameter: Vande Putte q and mass uncertainties
competing_evidence: VandePutte+03 Table 9 prints q=M2/M1=0.64±0.08 and M1=0.99±0.18 Msun; §4.2.1 prose prints q=0.64±0.36 and M1=0.99±0.30 Msun. Direct first-order propagation from Table 5 K1=92±3 and K2=144±18 km/s gives q=0.639±0.083, consistent with Table 9 but not the prose uncertainty.

parameter: WD temperature and conditional continuum temperature
competing_evidence: Linnell+10 Table 11 uses Teff(WD)=50,000 K, but §7/conclusion says the WD contribution is small and the data cannot determine Teff; Greenstein & Oke+82’s ~7,000 K blackbody and 400 pc distance are conditional on an F-star interpretation and may represent a cooler irradiated component.

needed_action: Keep the WD Teff as not directly determined; if a component temperature is needed, identify an independent WD-sensitive observation/model and distinguish it from disk/spot/irradiated-region temperatures.

competing_evidence: Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric posterior is 221.635 [220.657,222.708] pc; photogeometric posterior is 222.039 [220.696,223.129] pc. Hewitt+20 Gaia DR2 gives 236.5±5.0 pc; Beuermann+92 about 150 pc by Bailey method; Coppejans+15 lists 150±37 pc with its own conservative error; Linnell+10 Hipparcos value 289(+689/-119) pc; Greenstein & Oke+82’s 400 pc is conditional on an F-star interpretation. E(B−V) values/adoptions include <0.03, 0, 0.014, and 0.02.
why_it_matters: Distance and reddening affect absolute magnitudes, luminosities, and UV-derived Mdot branches.
needed_action: Use the Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior in the compatibility fields; retain historical/model branches. Before publishing extinction-corrected CMD values or selecting an Mdot branch, verify any independent parallax/extinction and the original Bailey-method details.

needed_action: Inspect the authors’ polarization calculation/Appendix or original data reduction; decide whether the source-level 12.9% claim can be assigned to either epoch. Wide-table per-epoch percent remains NA; absolute flux limits and source-level text claim are preserved separately.

parameter: X-ray band conversion and absorption convention
competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 lists 4.4±0.5e-12 erg cm−2 s−1 (1–10 keV) and 5.6±0.6e-12 (0.1–10 keV; 10% error-floor asterisk) with X-ray ref 9=Evans+20/2SXPS. needed_action: Retrieve the exact 2SXPS source record and reproduce the count-to-flux conversion/model/NH; until then retain as reported model-converted fluxes and do not label them unabsorbed or simultaneous.

parameter: tentative 6–7 min color timescale vs WD spin
competing_evidence: Greenstein & Oke+82 Appendix reports a “suggestion” of 6–7 min periodicity in a short 1973 U−V color series, with a hot-spot/disk-aspect interpretation; it also cites 600–1200 s variability from Hesser et al. 1972. No inspected follow-up paper establishes a coherent WD spin.
why_it_matters: Misclassifying a disk color timescale as a spin period would alter synchronization and magnetic-population comparisons.
needed_action: If a spin value is to be published, locate/reanalyze the original photometry and later timing literature; current spin field stays empty and the tentative range remains separately labeled.

competing_evidence: VandePutte+03 finds a best skew-map match to K5 template, with ~10% donor light near 8000 Å; its period relation expects K9±3. The paper notes template-grid/signal limitations. Donor masses differ by method: Beuermann ~0.62, VandePutte 0.75±0.35 from i/K1/K2, and 0.63±0.18 from the period–mass relation; Linnell adopts 0.674 from Knigge sequence.
why_it_matters: Donor spectral type, mass and temperature can be confused with template or population-sequence outputs.
needed_action: For a precise donor subtype/Teff or mass, obtain a higher-S/N donor-dominated spectrum or reconcile the original dynamical solution; do not convert K5/K9 into a measured Teff.

competing_evidence: Exact Gaia DR3 match has RUWE=1.088 but astrometric_excess_noise=0.1645 mas with significance 38.08; duplicated_source=false, 21 matched transits, 13 visibility periods, and phot_variable_flag=NOT_AVAILABLE.
why_it_matters: Formal parallax precision and CMD placement may understate unresolved-binary/systematic effects, though the counterpart identity is secure.
needed_action: Review any later independent astrometry or Gaia quality guidance before treating the posterior’s formal precision as the full uncertainty; preserve the current posterior and quality fields.

competing_evidence: Greenstein & Oke+82 estimates ~1e-8 Msun yr−1 (possibly 3e-8 under an alternate continuum assumption); Linnell+10 fits 5.75e-9 at 289 pc or 2e-9 at 150 pc; Hewitt+20 Table 4 selects 8e-9 from a simple blackbody disc model with fixed system inputs and says curves are not SED fits.
why_it_matters: Accretion-rate inference is distance/model dependent and could be mistaken for a directly measured transfer rate.
needed_action: Keep each method/distance branch separate; choose a value only for a stated modeling purpose and document adopted distance/WD mass/disk law. No value is selected in this audit.

competing_evidence: Rodríguez-Gil+09 finds significant circular polarization and argues the system is magnetic; Wörpel+20 finds no secure IP spin and favors non-magnetic; Bruch+23 adopts the non-magnetic interpretation.
why_it_matters: Changes population comparisons and the interpretation of the polarization signal.
needed_action: Decide whether to retain a disputed class or adopt a provisional magnetic/non-magnetic class after review of the original timing/polarimetry evidence.

competing_evidence: Rodríguez-Gil+09 19.38 +/- 0.39 min CP modulation could be 2(omega-Omega) or 2omega; Wörpel+20 1549 s signal is marginal (~1e-2) and phase folding limited.
why_it_matters: Spin assignment affects magnetic classification and WD spin comparisons.
needed_action: Check whether a later timing/polarimetry analysis resolves the mode assignment; do not fill the WD spin field until then.

competing_evidence: Patterson+02 establishes Porb=0.120560(14)d and reports negative superhump 0.11696d; Eq. 3 repeats an orbital epoch at HJD 2453383.813, 1000d later than Eq. 1. Bruch+23 gives TESS 0.11692d; Dağ+26 explicitly calls 2.807h a negative superhump.
why_it_matters: Confusing these signals would corrupt orbital-period and spin/beat comparisons.
needed_action: Verify Patterson Eq. 3 epoch against source errata or author record; preserve each period with its published interpretation.

competing_evidence: Mickaelian+02 p.1 printed DSS RA 16:43:49.71 is ~50 arcsec from Gaia/SIMBAD, while article states its candidate lies 7.2 arcsec from the X-ray position; exact SIMBAD identifiers link the V1084 Her, RX J, 1RXS and Gaia names.

needed_action: Check original journal scan or erratum for the printed coordinate; retain exact-name Gaia association unless contrary evidence emerges.

competing_evidence: Ak+08 Table 1 gives model distance 305 pc without an uncertainty. Coppejans+15 repeats 305 +/- 137 pc but footnote ordering assigns 45% uncertainty to V1084 Her and 25% to RW Sex, inconsistent with V1084 value if interpreted as stated. Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior median is 465.464 pc.

needed_action: Confirm Coppejans footnote ordering/possible typo; keep old model and Gaia posterior separate.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 gives approximate converted 1–10 and 0.1–10 keV fluxes but does not specify a V1084-specific absorption convention. Wörpel+20 provides an independent absorbed XMM fit and calls Table 6 flux/luminosity bolometric.
why_it_matters: Mixing absorbed, unabsorbed, band-limited and bolometric quantities biases X-ray comparisons.
needed_action: Retain records separately; confirm the conversion convention from Ridder supplementary material/source or 2SXPS model metadata.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 1 gives 0.1382009(4) d from Peters & Thorstensen+06; Arenas+00 reports an independent 0.1385±0.0002 d Hβ velocity period. Original P&T full table has not been retrieved; P&T abstract only confirms five old novae were studied.

needed_action: Retrieve and inspect P&T+06 V603 table/notes; confirm the 0.1382009(4) transcription and preserve any epoch/method difference.

parameter: distance and distance-dependent FUV accretion rates
competing_evidence: Harrison+13 HST-FGS parallax 4.011±0.137 mas and distance 249(+9/−8) pc; Gaia DR2 parallax 3.191±0.069 mas; Schaefer+18 reports 5.4σ disagreement and likely HST systematic error; Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric distance 315.407593 [311.865845,318.376343] pc. Sion+15 FUV models use the HST distance.
why_it_matters: Distance changes luminosities and inferred disk Mdot; old FUV solutions cannot be rescaled without a new fit.
needed_action: Retain all measurements separately; decide whether the Sion+15 FUV models should be re-fit at the Gaia posterior distance before using those Mdot values in population summaries.

competing_evidence: Barrett+17 Tables 3–4 list epoch-specific polarized-channel fluxes and Stokes-I image statistics for 13B-17A/B; Barrett+20 Table 1 gives 13B semester C/X summary values 22±3 and 32±7 μJy with high CP but no epoch mapping; Hewitt+20 notes flux-scale concerns for Barrett+17. These cannot safely be averaged or treated as independent epochs.

needed_action: Check NRAO archive calibrated visibility data or author clarification to map Barrett+20 summary rows to 13B-17A/B and resolve flux-calibration lineage; keep ledger values separate meanwhile.

competing_evidence: Arenas+00 reports q=0.24±0.05, M1=1.2±0.2 M_sun, M2=0.29±0.04 M_sun, i=13±2°; solution assumes Hβ semiamplitude traces the WD, empirical disk line-width/q relations, and a Roche-filling main-sequence donor. Sion+15 also uses M1 grid points; Retter & Naylor compile wider ranges.
why_it_matters: Treating a model-dependent solution as precise component measurements biases CV physical-property distributions.
needed_action: Decide whether these values remain tagged conditional/model-dependent in any community-facing aggregate; do not present them as direct component measurements.

competing_evidence: Barrett+20 gives radio-emission-region B=3210±365 G under a maser interpretation and discusses a possible donor-coronal origin; it separately argues a WD field, if present, must be <1 kG under disk-truncation assumptions. No direct WD surface field found; historical IP/spin claims are unconfirmed.
why_it_matters: Confusing radio-region B with WD surface B would change magnetic-CV classification and population comparisons.
needed_action: Keep the measurements in separate component/field columns; require direct Zeeman/cyclotron/WD-polar evidence before adopting a WD field.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 6.7±1.1×10−13 (1–10 keV) and 4.3±0.4×10−12 erg cm−2 s−1 (0.1–10 keV), derived from catalog information with generic model conversions; asterisk imposes a 10% error floor. Evans+20 is the underlying 2SXPS catalog, not the source-specific fit.
why_it_matters: Cross-population flux/luminosity comparisons can mix absorption conventions, bands and spectral assumptions.
needed_action: Verify the exact source-specific 2SXPS model/NH and Ridder conversion inputs or mark these values as approximate catalog estimates in downstream comparisons.

competing_evidence: Ridder+26 Table 3 and figures list V603 Aql on 2018-01-25; article text associates the epoch with ObsID 19A-166, which appears inconsistent with the calendar date/program context.
why_it_matters: The epoch matters for independent-observation counts and state matching.
needed_action: Resolve the VLA archive program/ObsID and correct the date or identifier if the paper has a transcription error.

competing_evidence: Patterson+97 revisits a historical 23.46(1) or 22.46(1) cycles d−1 claim; its own 1994 data include weak 22.390(5) and 22.82(2) cycles d−1 features, which may be harmonic/sideband or spin-related. Authors do not claim a secure WD rotation period; later X-ray/photometry does not establish an IP spin.
why_it_matters: A mistaken spin assignment would affect WD rotation and magnetic-class comparisons.
needed_action: Keep candidates out of the adopted spin field unless later timing/polarimetry uniquely resolves the frequency mode.

competing_evidence: Rodriguez+26 optical spectrum fit: 300±30 pc; deRuiter+25 broadband SED: 333±25 pc (337±25 with Gaia prior); Gaia EDR3 geometric 504 pc [395,652], photogeometric 710 pc [615,845].
why_it_matters: Distance changes luminosities, absolute magnitude and inferred radii; SED results lie below geometric parallax posterior.
needed_action: Choose display-distance convention or show Gaia posterior plus both SED fits; do not average.

competing_evidence: Published 125.52978±0.00002 min converts to 7531.7868±0.0012 s topocentric; Rodriguez cites a distinct 7531.1699±0.0012 s barycentric value from private communication; RV orbit 7530±390 s.
why_it_matters: Clock identity and synchronization affect polar/asynchronous interpretation.
needed_action: Verify/reprocess barycentric timing and obtain multi-night RV ephemeris; keep all periods separate meanwhile.

competing_evidence: M4.5V donor is spectroscopic; blue excess and DA+M fit favor a WD, but no direct WD Balmer/Zeeman/cyclotron signature or field measurement.
why_it_matters: Whether WD LPT classification is confirmed affects population counts; magnetic CV/WD-pulsar connection is not established.
needed_action: Retain “WD favored by SED; magnetic/polar status unconfirmed” unless direct WD evidence is judged sufficient.

competing_evidence: deRuiter+25 places pulses at donor superior conjunction; Rodriguez+26 finds phase 0.33–0.35, about 0.1 cycle after RV maximum, conditional on radio=orbital period.
why_it_matters: Phase relation constrains orbital gating versus independent spin clock and emission geometry.
needed_action: Resolve with phase-connected radio ephemeris and consecutive-night spectroscopy; retain both published results meanwhile.

competing_evidence: M4.5V is best but M4V not excluded. Rodriguez fixed log g=8 WD model, 10-Gyr solar Baraffe donor, 10% donor inflation and E(B−V)=0.01; Table 1 prints E(B−V)=0.01±0.001.
why_it_matters: Assumptions affect component parameters and comparison; extinction notation differs within paper.
needed_action: Keep outputs model-labeled; decide whether to record extinction as fixed or with table uncertainty.

competing_evidence: Rodriguez+25/+26 composite SED fit 380±10 pc; discovery YMW16 0.4±0.1 kpc and NE2001 1.8±0.5 kpc then adopted 1.5±0.5 kpc; exact Gaia DR3 parallax −0.223±0.981 mas yields Bailer-Jones geometric 3.010 [1.566,6.045] kpc and photogeometric 3.859 [3.273,4.252] kpc.
