needed_action: Decide whether 380 pc remains the compatibility display as a model-dependent SED distance while all alternatives are shown, and verify which Bailer-Jones posterior Rodriguez+25 intended (or whether its text is a typo). Do not average the methods.

competing_evidence: M-dwarf RV orbit and blue continuum favor a compact WD; Rodriguez+25/+26 fit a DA WD+M model and argue against an NS, but no WD Balmer/Zeeman/cyclotron signature or WD field is directly measured. Radio coherency motivates magnetism but does not measure it.
why_it_matters: A confirmed-WD versus WD-favored label affects RAWDOG population counts and comparison with magnetic CVs/WD pulsars.
needed_action: Choose whether the WD+M composite-spectrum inference qualifies for the confirmed-WD sample, or should remain a favored/inferred WD classification pending direct WD evidence; retain magnetic/polar status as unconfirmed meanwhile.

parameter: radio recurrence, orbit, spin and long timing term
competing_evidence: Radio recurrence 10496.5522±0.0008 s; two-night RV orbit 10496±5 s (one-night 10500±500 s). The ~6.27±0.23 yr sinusoid with 60.5±11.2 light-second projected amplitude may be timing noise or orbital/super-orbital motion. The fitted radio Pdot includes zero; 3σ upper limit <3.9e−11 s/s.
why_it_matters: Treating radio recurrence as WD spin or the long sinusoid as an orbit would change magnetic/synchronization and evolutionary interpretation.
needed_action: Keep recurrence and RV orbit as separate measurements; decide only after phase-connected timing clarifies the long-term residuals whether any spin or additional orbit is supported.

parameter: SED component values and reddening assumptions
competing_evidence: WD/donor temperatures, radii, WD mass, distance, q, inclination and filling factor come from a composite MCMC model: DA Koester log g=8, BT-DUSTY solar log g=5, 10-Gyr Baraffe donor, imposed 10% radius inflation, and E(B−V) tied to Edenhofer dust map. A fixed E(B−V)=0.3 branch lowers the fitted WD mass from 1.02 to 0.82 M_sun.
why_it_matters: These are model-dependent component estimates, not independent dynamical measurements or Gaia single-star parameters.
needed_action: Keep each quantity tagged as an SED/model result with the assumptions and alternative extinction branch; decide whether the data-dictionary category should call these inferred rather than measured component properties.

competing_evidence: Rodriguez+25 finds weak H-alpha with a possible ~330 km/s component outside the M dwarf, but only one orbit of spectra was available and chromospheric activity remains an alternative; Rodriguez+26 retains the need for follow-up.
why_it_matters: The line origin bears on accretion state and whether the radio source is interacting through a compact-object magnetosphere.
needed_action: Obtain multi-epoch phase-resolved H-alpha spectroscopy; leave accretion or magnetic-channeling interpretation unresolved.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 LOFAR position is 16:34:30 +44:50:10 (±2 arcsec, stated 3 sigma); its GALEX FUV candidate is 0.57 arcsec away and UNIONS detections are nearby. Dong+25 VLA position is 16:34:29.96 +44:50:13.5 (reported 1-sigma upper uncertainties 0.5 and 1.1 arcsec), about 3.53 arcsec from the LOFAR position. The FUV candidate is about 4.08 arcsec from the VLA center. Dong+25 HSC source lies outside 2 sigma but within 3 sigma, is classified extended, has 5.8% chance alignment, and lacks GALEX UV detection. A 0.46 arcsec/yr scale over the 2016–2023 interval is within Bloot+25’s <1 arcsec/yr limit, but no proper motion is measured. Gaia DR3 query finds no source inside 18.006 arcsec.
why_it_matters: Association of the optical/UV candidate determines whether the WD evidence can be used and whether any Gaia/CMD information belongs to this system.
needed_action: Keep Gaia ID unassigned. Obtain high-resolution, multi-epoch astrometry and deeper UV/optical imaging/spectroscopy tied to the VLA position; determine whether the GALEX/UNIONS and HSC sources are the same object and whether either is physically associated.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 argues for a WD-containing system from marginal GALEX/UNIONS photometry and a conditional WD SED fit. Dong+25 finds the HSC source potentially extended with 5.8% chance alignment, no GALEX UV detection, and argues the high circular polarization, radio energy and microstructure are more pulsar-like; active magnetars are constrained by X-rays but NS-like alternatives remain.
why_it_matters: Classification affects whether this source belongs in a WD-hosting subset and any comparison with CVs or WD pulsars.
needed_action: Retain LPT as confirmed and WD host as candidate. Seek secure optical/UV counterpart, spectroscopy, parallax, or other component-specific evidence before promoting the WD classification.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 measures an 841.24808 s pulse clock, a 4206.2406 s alternative interpulse timing solution, and proposes 2103.1061–2103.1141 s or 1402.0814–1402.0853 s orbital periods in 5:2/5:3 models. Dong+25 measures 841.245895 s with a significant negative derivative and a ~4206 s burst-arrival pattern, but states there is no evidence for the specific 2103 s orbit. Zhan+26 instead treats 841 s as orbit and 4206 s as spin-orbit beat in a double-WD model.
why_it_matters: Confusing spin, orbital, beat, interpulse and burst-recurrence clocks would create a false Porb or evolutionary interpretation.
needed_action: Keep all clocks separate and Porb unset. Confirm with a phase-coherent secondary-clock measurement, optical spectroscopy/eclipses, or independently measured orbital motion.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 DM=22.5±5.5 pc cm−3 gives 1.0–1.6 kpc with NE2001 and 1.5–4.3 kpc with YMW16. Dong+25 mean DM=25.0±0.2 gives 1.4 and 3.0 kpc with the same respective models. No Gaia parallax or independent distance is available.
why_it_matters: Distance controls luminosity estimates and the conditional WD/companion SED solutions.
needed_action: Keep model-specific estimates separate. Revise only after a secure counterpart and parallax, or a better calibrated distance method, is available.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 Table 1 lists 383±52 mJy and its note calls this Stokes V. Detailed Table 2 gives 383±52 mJy in Stokes I and −346±33 mJy in Stokes V for the 2016-05-19 pulse. The catalog value matches Table 2 Stokes I, not the Table 1 Stokes-V label.
why_it_matters: A Stokes mislabel would distort polarization fraction and radio-flux comparisons.
needed_action: Preserve both table values in the ledger and label the compatibility flux as Stokes I from Table 2; check for a published correction or author clarification before changing the adopted component.

competing_evidence: Bloot+25 gives Teff=15,000–33,000 K and MWD≥0.78 Msun only if the marginal UV/optical detections are a homogeneous-surface WD SED; it quotes a lower distance bound >1.9 kpc. Dong+25 allows ~20,000–40,000 K only if the HSC source is real. Bloot+25 abstract/conclusion says earlier than M7 is ruled out, while §4.1 says M6 is excluded at 4.3 kpc and Figure 9 makes the limit distance dependent.
why_it_matters: Treating these conditional fits or companion templates as measured component properties would overstate what the data establish.
needed_action: Keep temperatures/mass as conditional model rows, not adopted direct values. Resolve counterpart identity and use Figure 9 with any justified distance before quoting a single companion spectral-type cutoff.

competing_evidence: Rose+26 gives a broad parallax posterior 570(+620/-190) pc and a Bailer-Jones photogeometric posterior 6500(+2600/-1100) pc, then adopts 400–9100 pc; Knigge+26 v1 obtains 322(+70/-61) pc from a two-component SED. Imbrogno+26 uses 570 pc for luminosities. Gaia parallax S/N is only about 1.9 and astrometric excess noise is 3.84 mas with RUWE 1.996.
why_it_matters: Luminosities, radio power, absolute magnitude and inferred system scale vary strongly with distance; the photogeometric prior may be biased by binary/accretion light.
needed_action: Keep all methods and the broad range separate. Before publishing a preferred point distance or component CMD position, verify with improved astrometry or resolved component photometry; do not invert the low-S/N parallax as a precise distance.

competing_evidence: Nature main text/abstract gives G=19.45+/-0.04, Methods gives 19.40+/-0.04, and Supplementary Table 1 gives 19.64+/-0.039; exact Gaia DR3 ID query gives 19.449984+/-0.039153. BP-RP=1.079 is flagged by BP/RP excess factor 2.894 and the neighbor 0.9 arcsec away.
why_it_matters: A mistaken G input shifts absolute magnitude/SED scale; blended BP/RP color can misplace the system on a CMD and be mistaken for an intrinsic component color.
needed_action: Use exact Gaia G as the catalog photometry value while preserving the manuscript conflict. Keep BP/RP as observed blended values and exclude them from intrinsic-color/CMD interpretation unless a resolved/deblended measurement is verified.

parameter: UV extinction correction and WD temperature
competing_evidence: Rose+26 published UV table has FUV/NUV=21.36/21.36 AB after the notebook multiplies observed flux by CCM89 attenuation, which dims it. The authors' 2026-07-06 public code commit adds corrected inputs FUV=18.31 and NUV=17.97 and loads that CSV in the fitting notebook; its cached blackbody output is 36460+/-7304 K, chi2_red=11.74. The published Rose fit is 26641+/-4139 K, chi2_red=4.27. Knigge+26 v1 DA SED fit gives 14500(+5000/-1200) K with different photometry/model assumptions. No formal journal correction/replacement fit was located.
why_it_matters: The UV input correction materially changes the fitted hot-component temperature; none of these broad-band blackbody/SED values is a direct WD photospheric measurement.
needed_action: Retain the published value and post-publication corrected-input/cached result as separate records. Before adopting a single Teff, verify whether the repository correction is author-approved as a replacement result and obtain a clean, preferably spectroscopic or UV-atmosphere analysis with deblended inputs.

parameter: donor mass, temperature and evolutionary state
competing_evidence: Rose+26 period-density relation gives M2=0.0963+/-0.0047 Msun (Methods rounds to 0.096+/-0.008) and empirical M6–M6.5/~2800 K; Knigge+26 v1 SED fit gives 0.052+/-0.008 Msun and ~1800 K by constraining the donor to a semi-empirical CV sequence. No donor absorption spectrum or dynamical mass is available.
why_it_matters: The competing model values differ across the hydrogen-burning boundary and change conclusions about period-bouncer status and donor evolution.
needed_action: Keep both model families separate and label assumptions. Resolve only with donor spectroscopy, dynamical constraints or independently validated resolved near-IR data; do not silently select the lower-error or newer estimate.

competing_evidence: SOAR emission-line RVs give Porb=1.368+/-0.053 h; phase-connected radio recurrence is 4841.89(+0.12/-0.14) s; X-ray period is 4868+/-22 s. These are broadly consistent but no separate WD spin is identified. Radio cutoff modulation ~29 ks and X-ray long modulation 52+/-2 ks are distinct and poorly constrained. Rose defers polar/asynchronous-polar/IP subtype; Imbrogno discusses IP/asynchronous-polar behavior.
why_it_matters: Equating recurrence/orbital/spin/beat clocks would create a false synchronization or evolutionary classification.
needed_action: Retain spectroscopic Porb as the compatibility orbital value and keep each clock separately labeled. Resolve spin/subtype with long-baseline phase-resolved spectroscopy/polarimetry or a distinct stable spin signal.

parameter: WD component properties and magnetic field
competing_evidence: No direct WD spectrum, dynamic WD mass, cooling age, or Zeeman/cyclotron surface-field measurement was found. Rose adopts MWD=0.83+/-0.23 Msun as a CV mean; Knigge fixes 0.8 Msun. Imbrogno's kT=0.14 keV and ~1 km radius are a small accretion component. Rose's >0.96 kG is a conditional local radio-emission-region bound; its MG dipole is a chosen model.
why_it_matters: Model priors, plasma temperatures and radio-emission-site fields can be mistaken for WD mass, photospheric temperature, radius or surface field.
needed_action: Continue to mark these as priors/model outputs. A direct component claim needs WD-atmosphere/spectropolarimetric data and an independently constrained binary mass function.

competing_evidence: Knigge+26 reports Gaussian versus Moffat PSF magnitudes differing by 0.2–0.6 mag; the neighbor is brighter and fit diagnostics show only slight elongation toward the target. Their formal errors are 0.1–0.2 mag and do not encompass this systematic; a false deblend remains possible.
why_it_matters: The Ks flux drives the brown-dwarf donor mass/temperature in the SED fit.
needed_action: Keep both PSF solutions with methods and uncertainties. Verify with higher-resolution resolved near-IR imaging/spectroscopy before treating Ks flux or the donor component as established.

competing_evidence: Knigge+26 v1 calls the system likely post-period-minimum based on the donor-sequence-constrained SED mass; its own paper notes Porb=1.368+/-0.053 h can be pre- or post-minimum. Rose+26's Roche period-density donor estimate is above the sub-stellar boundary. The accreting magnetic-CV/LPT classification itself is secure.
why_it_matters: This distinction materially changes claims about evolutionary pathways connecting CVs, WD pulsars and LPTs; the catalog must not encode a model claim as an established sequence.
needed_action: Keep 'period bouncer' as a proposed model interpretation only. Do not claim a unique evolutionary pathway without an independently secure donor mass/state and comparative population evidence.

parameter: K-band radio significance and radio-emission-site interpretation
competing_evidence: Barrett+20 Table 1: X-band Stokes I 79±14 μJy (~5.6σ); K-band 49±29 μJy (~1.7σ) but composite S/N=4.5. Table 2 7530±365 G assumes fundamental donor-coronal ECM; §4.2 also discusses accretion-column sites.
why_it_matters: Counting a marginal K point as a second secure detection, or treating a conditional kG plasma field as a WD surface field, affects radio-incidence and field-population comparisons.
needed_action: If band-specific incidence or source-site claims are needed, inspect/reprocess VLA visibility/source-finding products and confirm K-band Stokes-I significance and centroid. Until then preserve the reported point and composite S/N separately; keep ECM/donor-corona B conditional.

parameter: Historical cyclotron field and optical circular polarization from Szkody+05
competing_evidence: Kolbin+23 full text states Szkody+05 cyclotron harmonics correspond to 44 MG and optical circular polarization reached 30%; Dillon+08 full text independently describes cyclotron humps and up to -30% optical CP, citing Szkody+05. The accessible Szkody abstract confirms spectropolarimetry established a polar but gives no field value. Direct ADS PDF returned HTTP 403 and publisher PDF endpoint returned anti-bot HTML.
why_it_matters: Historical field affects comparison with the newer 28.5±1.5 MG mean photospheric field and ~34 MG local cyclotron spot; original field component, harmonic assignment, phase/state and uncertainty remain unverified.
needed_action: If this historical comparison is needed for a paper or population analysis, provide/access Szkody et al. (2005) full text and verify its FR Lyn spectrum, table/figure, polarization sign/phase, and field derivation. Until then retain 44 MG as a secondary-reported value only; do not select or average it.
public_status: Awaiting access to the original source

parameter: Orbital eclipse-timing interpretation and period derivative
competing_evidence: Schwarz+09 Table 2a provides poor linear, quadratic (Pdot=-7.3e-12 s/s), sinusoidal (~13 yr), and combined fits; Bours+14 §5.2 gives a quadratic Pdot=-5.2e-12 s/s but rejects the old single-planet solution and finds no unique fit to all data; Schwope & Thinius+18 publisher abstract (full text inaccessible) says the steep 2010-2013 O-C decline slowed before mid-2016. The timings are accretion-spot egress markers and can move with spot/state changes.
why_it_matters: A secular orbital derivative materially affects evolutionary comparisons and a planet/Applegate interpretation is not established by these timing fits.
needed_action: Keep the Bours+14 reference ephemeris period for catalog indexing, but do not use a single Pdot in population analysis until full Schwope & Thinius+18 data/fit context and the timing-marker systematics are reviewed; choose whether population plots should show only P_orb or separately tagged model-dependent Pdot candidates.

competing_evidence: Watson+03 Table 3 prints q=0.25 with M1=0.61 and M2=0.15 Msun, numerically consistent with M2/M1; the paper's method prose defines the opposite convention in one place. §7.2 compares the q=0.25 reconstruction with Heerlein and Schwope values, while Schwope+11 and Schwope+25 explicitly define Q=MWD/M2≈4.6.
why_it_matters: A silently inverted ratio can corrupt binary mass-ratio comparisons and period-dependent donor analysis.
needed_action: Keep Watson's printed q=0.25 and masses as separate historical table values without adopting or inverting the ratio; decide whether the codebook should label its convention unresolved or annotate the likely M2/M1 interpretation.

competing_evidence: Ferrario+15 Table 2 lists BZeem,phot=20: MG and cites Schwope+93a, Schwope+97 and Glenn+94b in the HU Aqr row; the colon marks an uncertain secondary-table value. The primary cyclotron/accretion-region field from Schwope+03 is near 34 MG, and Ferrario+15 separately lists Bcyc1=37 MG.
why_it_matters: Photospheric Zeeman and accretion-region cyclotron fields are different diagnostics; mixing them changes the inferred WD field and population comparison.
needed_action: Locate the original spectrum/source behind the Ferrario+15 20: MG table entry, inspect its component and method, and adopt it only if a primary photospheric field result is confirmed; otherwise retain as secondary-only/unresolved.

parameter: Ridder+23 compiled X-ray flux source-state/spectrum mapping
competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 3 gives 3.3e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 (1-10 keV) and 5.4e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 (0.1-10 keV) without per-row uncertainties or an explicit HU Aqr epoch/model mapping. Schwarz+09 reports epoch-resolved unabsorbed bolometric XMM fluxes: intermediate-state soft/hard components substantially brighter than low-state October 2003 and May 2005 values.
why_it_matters: These flux products have different energy bands, state, and absorption/bolometric conventions; substituting one for another can misstate the accretion state or X-ray luminosity.
needed_action: Trace Ridder+23's HU Aqr Table 3 inputs to the exact XMM observation/model and record its bandpass, absorption convention and uncertainty if recoverable; until then preserve compiled and epoch-specific values separately.

competing_evidence: Hoard+01 abstract reports candidate periods 0.1344 d and 0.2683 d and explicitly leaves the true orbital period ambiguous. Woudt & Warner+02 §2.7 favors the longer double-wave/ellipsoidal interpretation and gives 0.2689 +/-0.0007 d; Rawls et al. AAS abstract reports 0.2683 d.
why_it_matters: The orbital period controls population placement and any period/evolution comparisons; the short and long aliases differ by a factor of two.
needed_action: If adopting 6.4536 h as the preferred orbit, confirm that the double-wave interpretation is sufficient despite the inaccessible full Hoard+01 article; otherwise publish both candidate aliases without a canonical scalar.

competing_evidence: Froning+12 and Hewitt+20 call CM Phe NL; Hewitt+20 §§2.11/4.3 says likely DN with missed outbursts because of faint absolute magnitude and sparse long-term light curve; Rawls et al. AAS abstract reports nine-year VY Scl-like luminosity changes possibly due to mass-transfer changes.
why_it_matters: Subtype affects comparison of accretion state and radio limits among non-magnetic CVs. The evidence does not establish a unique subtype or evolutionary path.
needed_action: Choose whether the online/catalog grouping should retain NL as historical discovery class with a “likely DN / VY Scl-like behavior” qualifier, or use a broader uncertain-CV subtype. Full Rawls dataset/paper would resolve the reported long-term behavior.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Methods describes 856 MHz bandwidth centered at 1.284 GHz (nominal 0.856-1.712 GHz); Ridder+23 Table 4 labels 0.43-2.1 GHz.
why_it_matters: Bandpass labels affect comparison of spectral behavior and radio luminosity across catalog populations.
needed_action: Use MeerKAT configured band 0.856-1.712 GHz for the observation row; check whether Ridder+23 intended a broader comparison interval or contains a table error before retaining its band as a system-level value.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 prints flux density <30 uJy and specific luminosity <4.6e15 erg s-1 Hz-1; the paper gives d=315.1 pc and Lnu=4πd²Fnu, which yields about 3.56e15. With preferred EDR3 d=308.39825 pc, the same flux limit yields 3.41e15.
why_it_matters: Radio luminosity limits are used in population comparisons; a mismatch changes the limit by about 30% and may indicate an unstated flux threshold or a table calculation error.
needed_action: Check Hewitt+20’s image RMS/peak map and exact unrounded 3-sigma limit or author-calculation convention; until then retain the published 4.6e15 and locally reproducible values as separate claims, without selecting one as verified.

competing_evidence: Hoard+01 abstract and Hewitt+20 report M2-5 spectral type from TiO. Hewitt+20 §4.5 assumes M2=0.5 Msun (roughly M0) for an SED model because the model is insensitive to donor mass and invokes a possibly evolved donor.
why_it_matters: The assumed mass is not a measured donor mass and is not straightforwardly matched to the M2-5 spectrum; component mass/evolution comparisons would be biased if the model input is used as a measurement.
needed_action: Keep the 0.5 Msun value only as a model assumption unless the primary spectroscopy/dynamical source is recovered; verify whether the spectral type and model donor assumption can be reconciled by the evolved-donor interpretation.

competing_evidence: Hoard+01 and Hoard & Wachter+98 full text were inaccessible (abstract/secondary reporting only); Hewitt+20 cites Jaidee & Lynga 1969 for the corrected historical identification but its original text was not retrieved. Exact SIMBAD/Gaia DR3 identifier membership independently secures the current counterpart.
why_it_matters: Detailed photometric alias interpretation, original donor spectral classification, and historical identity correction have a weaker citation chain than the later measurements.
needed_action: If community-facing text needs the original evidence, obtain Hoard+01/Hoard & Wachter+98/Jaidee & Lynga+69 full texts and verify the exact photometric/spectroscopic/identity chain. Current Gaia counterpart assignment does not depend on resolving the 1969 paper.

competing_evidence: 2SXPS exact source products give 0.3-10 keV observed/unabsorbed power-law catalogue fluxes; Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1-10 and 0.1-10 keV converted unabsorbed comparison fluxes with a minimum 10% error floor. The soft-band value extrapolates below Swift/XRT 0.3 keV coverage; none is simultaneous with 2019 radio.
why_it_matters: X-ray/radio comparisons are sensitive to bandpass, absorption correction, spectral assumptions, and epoch/state.
needed_action: Before deriving an X-ray luminosity or comparing with radio, choose a uniform spectrum/band and epoch treatment or retain each as a separate model-dependent estimate; do not treat Table 4 values as native Evans fluxes.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 1 reports V=14.8-15.8 and M_V=7.3-8.3, but gives no explicit extinction correction/method in the table; numerical ranges resemble a distance-modulus transform using 315.1 pc.
why_it_matters: Absolute magnitude is used to argue for a low-state/faint DN interpretation; an unreported extinction correction or state selection can affect subtype inference.
needed_action: Recover Hewitt+20 calculation or source VSX photometry and extinction convention before treating M_V range as corrected physical luminosity; retain as published apparent-derived estimate only.

competing_evidence: Buckley+90 q=.46+/-.04, i=87+/-3 deg, M1=1.2+/-.1 Msun uses empirical M2~.55 and emission K=134+/-9 as WD motion. Thoroughgood+05 uncorrected branch gives q=.73+/-.05, i=85.0+/-2.1, M1=.73+/-.05, M2=.54+/-.06; corrected donor-line branch gives q=.83+/-.05, i=84.0+/-2.3, M1=.63+/-.04, M2=.52+/-.06. q=M2/M1.
why_it_matters: Component masses and q are central to population/evolution comparisons; methods and assumptions differ.
needed_action: Choose whether compatibility values should use the later donor-line irradiation-corrected branch with historical alternatives retained, or expose no canonical branch. Do not average.

competing_evidence: Buckley+90 calls IP/DQ Her speculative, partly from Lx/Lopt~4; CP<.5% rules out a polar but leaves IP possible. Hewitt+20 reports no coherent optical pulsations and no strong magnetic evidence. non_magnetic_cv is not measured B=0.
why_it_matters: Class assignment affects comparison across magnetic and non-magnetic populations; neither IP nor zero field is established.
needed_action: Decide whether public class remains non_magnetic_cv with explicit historical IP caveat or uses a broader CV/magnetic-status-uncertain label.

competing_evidence: Thoroughgood+05 best-fit template M0.5V and calls possible evolution tentative. It reports Diaz & Hubeny+99 as K0-K5V/possible later subgiant; original full text was inaccessible.
why_it_matters: Donor type/evolution affects interpretation of the low donor mass and period comparisons.
needed_action: If one subtype is needed, retain M0.5V as checked template result and mark K0-K5/subgiant as unresolved secondary report until Diaz & Hubeny+99 is checked.

competing_evidence: Buckley+90 174-380 pc; Thoroughgood+05 490+/-130 pc from donor light/main-sequence MV and E(B-V)=.05; it reports Mauche+94 340-590 and Diaz & Hubeny+99 510+/-160. Hewitt+20 Gaia DR2 295.8+/-1.4; exact BJ EDR3 geometric posterior 290.347565 [289.274597,291.501740]. Methods differ.
why_it_matters: Distance affects radio/X-ray luminosity and absolute magnitude; older donor/extinction estimates are model dependent.
needed_action: Keep EDR3 geometric posterior in current fields and preserve historical estimates. Confirm this preferred choice for public use; do not average estimates.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 <30 microJy, RMS 10 microJy and Lnu<3.1e15. Section 4.1 rejects 28+/-14 microJy: below 5 sigma, offset ~2 arcsec, beam-inconsistent. Setup is 856 MHz centered 1.284 GHz (0.856-1.712); Ridder+23 labels 0.43-2.1.
why_it_matters: A false detection or band mismatch affects radio-emitter and spectral comparisons.
needed_action: Use nondetection and primary configured band 0.856-1.712 GHz; preserve Ridder band as discrepancy until intent is known.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 has 1-10 flux 1.7+/-0.4e-13 and 0.1-10 2.1+/-0.6e-13. Its section 3.2 describes 2SXPS hardness/model conversions. Exact 2SXPS 142122 has observed 0.3-10 PowFlux 1.248+/-0.331e-13 and unabsorbed 2.474+/-0.656e-13. 0.1-10 extrapolates below Swift/XRT 0.3 keV; historical HEAO flux was transient/high.
why_it_matters: X-ray/radio comparisons depend on band, absorption, spectrum, state and epoch.
needed_action: Keep native and converted values separate; choose uniform comparison band/model/state treatment. Trace exact Ridder object-level conversion if possible.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 4 lists Mdot=6e-9 Msun/yr; section 4.5 says rate was varied and selected by visual SED resemblance, not fit, with WD/donor light omitted.
why_it_matters: Model input could be mistaken for measured Mdot in accretion/evolution comparisons.
needed_action: Retain only as an SED-model-selected rate unless an independent direct Mdot estimate is located.

competing_evidence: Thoroughgood+05 full text checked; Diaz & Hubeny+99 and Mauche+94 original full texts not retrieved. Still+98 publisher metadata/abstract checked; its full article not independently read. Related claims are secondary reports.
why_it_matters: Donor subtype, distance/extinction and spiral claims have weaker provenance than directly checked mass/orbit/radio papers.
needed_action: Obtain and check Diaz & Hubeny+99 and Mauche+94 original tables if needed for public claims; otherwise retain as explicitly secondary.

competing_evidence: Echevarria+07 adopts optical H-alpha wing K1=107±2 km/s and K2=310±5 with i=69.7±0.7, giving M1=1.20±0.05 Msun. Long & Gilliland+99 abstract reports GHRS photospheric K1=107.1±2.1 and M1=1.12 Msun for i=67°, K2=294.7. Naylor+05 gives M1=0.91±0.01/sin^3(i), or 1.02–1.32 Msun for i=62–74°, but omits K2 systematics. Unda-Sanzana+06 optical spectra produce K1 estimates 80–~150 and cannot recover 107; they identify bright-spot asymmetry at high velocities.
why_it_matters: WD mass and q inform population comparisons, but the H-alpha tracer and uncertainty assumptions are disputed; choosing one value silently would overstate precision.
needed_action: For community display, decide whether to expose all conditional branches without a canonical M1, or choose a provisional solution and document which velocity/inclination evidence is prioritized. Obtain Long & Gilliland full scanned article if its detailed model assumptions are needed.

competing_evidence: Naylor+05 FUV/parallax photometric radius is 5.7±0.4×10^8 cm; Long+06 FUSE uniform-WD Obs.1 model gives 5.0±0.2×10^8 cm at log g=8.5 (4.8–5.3×10^8 across log g=9–8) and 3.4×10^8 at log g=8.5 in Obs.2. Naylor+05 gravitational-redshift/inclination branch gives 4.13±0.44×10^8 cm at the lowest i and remains inconsistent by about 2.5σ. WD Teff also changes with outburst state and assumed gravity; 60–70 kK belt is non-unique.
why_it_matters: A single radius or temperature could mix different epochs and model branches and misrepresent WD structure/cooling.
needed_action: Keep state-specific model outputs and radius methods separate; if the wide table needs one scalar, decide whether to leave it blank or identify an explicitly provisional branch.

competing_evidence: Echevarria+07 TiO template fit is M6 V (~5% light in fitted region). Naylor+05 best spectroscopic templates are M4–M5 but mass/radius/luminosity/photometric temperature compare to M2; high metallicity is proposed as an explanation, not measured. Long & Gilliland+99 calls donor M4 in abstract.
why_it_matters: Donor subtype/evolution comparisons can be biased if a template fit or mass-sequence inference is treated as an intrinsic measured type.
needed_action: For catalog display, decide whether to show the competing spectral diagnostics in separate fields and leave intrinsic donor Teff/type unselected; no numeric Teff was found in the checked papers.

competing_evidence: Gaia DR3 parallax is 10.704757±0.033765 mas and Bailer-Jones geometric posterior is 93.057 pc [92.720,93.367], but RUWE=2.406, astrometric excess noise=0.229934 mas with significance=45.58, and Gaia marks photometry variable. HST/FGS original 1999 parallax is 10.37±0.50 mas (96.4±4.6 pc); Harrison & Johnson+04 Table 3 gives a later 9.96±0.37 mas, corresponding to 100.4±3.7 pc as cited by Long+06. The differences are modest but Gaia formal precision should not be read without quality context.
why_it_matters: Distance affects unresolved M_G, radio/X-ray luminosities, and UV WD-radius normalization; RUWE/excess-noise may make formal posterior precision optimistic.
needed_action: Decide whether Bailer-Jones geometric posterior remains the compatibility distance with a prominent quality caveat, or whether the catalog should expose Gaia and HST values as co-equal alternatives. Do not average them.

competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 §4.2 states the shortest significant variation is 69 min and reports 27.0±7.7 μJy followed by <17.5 μJy. Table A1 lists two adjacent Obs.2 bins at MJD 57080.15979 and 57080.17264, each 1110 s, with 27.0±7.7 μJy then <23.7 μJy; their midpoint separation is 1110 s (18.5 min). Table 3 gives whole Obs.2 <16.8 μJy.
why_it_matters: The variability timescale and limit affect radio duty-cycle and cross-population comparisons.
needed_action: Retain both the paper’s 69-min prose claim and the exact table bins; verify from original visibility timestamps or author clarification before publishing a single variability timescale.

competing_evidence: Long+06 says reddening is not directly measured, cites Verbunt+87 E(B−V)=0 with upper limit 0.03 from absent 2200 Å feature, and assumes negligible reddening from NH. Harrison & Johnson+04 assumes AV=0 for outburst photometry. Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot returns AG=0.4338 and E(BP−RP)=0.2376, but its single-star model is inappropriate for this unresolved variable CV. The inherited Gaia GSP-Phot distance (94.3003 pc, bounds 93.91–94.61 pc) and Teff=4481.9 K are also single-star model outputs and are excluded from component values; the prior M_G derived from that distance is retained only as a superseded legacy calculation.
why_it_matters: Dereddening changes CMD interpretation; Gaia model extinction must not be substituted for a measured binary reddening.
needed_action: Keep M_G explicitly uncorrected and decide whether to publish no intrinsic color/M_G until original reddening evidence and an appropriate binary treatment are reviewed. Do not interpret GSP-Phot distance or Teff as CV component measurements; keep them in explicit pipeline-output fields only.

competing_evidence: Long & Gilliland+99 and Marsh+90 primary abstracts were checked but their complete original scanned articles were not accessible in this pass; exact orbital period is visible in Echevarria+07 and Coppejans+16, while Long & Gilliland masses/K1 are quoted by Naylor+05 and the abstract. Historical 1977/1980s radio upper limits are summarized in Coppejans+16 but their original reports were not individually read.
why_it_matters: Detailed original timing, calibration, and historical radio-limit methods cannot be fully checked from abstracts/secondary quotations.
needed_action: If those values are needed for release-level claims, obtain the original scanned Long & Gilliland and Marsh papers and the historical radio reports; otherwise keep the stated access limitations in the public provenance record.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1–10 and 0.1–10 keV fluxes from approximate 4XMM-DR11 conversions (full band minus soft bands for 1–10; full 0.2–12 used as approximate 0.1–10). Errors are raised to at least 10% and star-marked. A source-specific absorption convention/fit is not given, and radio observations are non-simultaneous.
why_it_matters: X-ray/radio ratios depend on bandpass, spectral model, absorption convention, and state.
needed_action: Keep these as approximate catalog-comparison fluxes; before luminosity/population comparison, choose a common X-ray band/model and retain an explicit absorption convention or return to native 4XMM products.

competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 finds the sample more consistent with synchrotron than coherent emission from low polarization, but U Gem had insufficient S/N for a spectral index and no source-specific mechanism is established. Its 1977/1980s upper limits are secondary summaries only; original reports were not retrieved.
why_it_matters: Mechanism labels can prematurely connect non-magnetic CV radio emission to a specific jet or evolutionary pathway; old limits have weaker provenance.
needed_action: Retain mechanism as an interpretation, not a measurement; inspect original older radio references only if those historical limits are used quantitatively.

competing_evidence: Shafter & Hessman (1988) state YZ Cnc does not eclipse; van Paradijs+94 does not establish eclipses. Coppejans+16 §2.4 calls it eclipsing, while Table 1 gives i=15 deg from Patterson+11; Harrison+04 Table 3 lists 38 +/-10 deg cited to Shafter & Hessman, and Patterson+11 Table 1 uses rough i≈40 deg.
why_it_matters: Inclination and eclipse geometry affect physical parameter inference, orbital phasing and comparison of radio emission with the binary plane.
needed_action: For community display, decide whether to publish all conflicting claims without a canonical eclipse/inclination classification, or commission a targeted reanalysis of original photometry and ephemerides.

competing_evidence: Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior 233.49 pc (p16 231.68, p84 235.03); ground parallax 4.4 +/-1.7 mas and Bayesian 222(+50/-42) pc; HST parallax 3.34 +/-0.45 mas with LK-corrected distance ~320 +/-40 pc; K-band template lower bound >=290 pc; Dhillon+00 secondarily quotes ~130 pc from Patterson+84.
why_it_matters: Distance controls luminosities and absolute magnitudes; several methods have different assumptions and one old estimate is secondary-only.
needed_action: Adopt Gaia geometric posterior as current catalog distance while keeping alternatives; if a single community luminosity is needed, decide whether to retain Gaia only or show method-separated historical estimates. Retrieve/recheck Patterson+84 original before using its ~130 pc claim.

competing_evidence: Shafter & Hessman+88 infer q≈0.22, M2≈0.17 Msun and likely M1≈0.75–0.90 under an H-alpha K1 relation; Zhao+05 report q=0.28±0.03, M1=0.46±0.06 and M2=0.13±0.01 using H-beta velocity/superhump calibration; Dai+26 derive q=0.175±0.011 from the newer epsilon(q) relation. None is a dynamical mass ratio.
why_it_matters: WD/donor masses and q drive evolutionary and population comparisons; a canonical branch would materially affect interpretation.
needed_action: Keep model/calibration branches separate and unselected until a dynamical q or improved phase-resolved component-velocity solution is available; if a provisional value is needed, specify calibration and systematic budget.

competing_evidence: Patterson+79 timing during the 1978 supermaximum changes from about 0.09204 d early to 0.0905 d late; Zhao+05 use historical 0.09204 d; Dai+26 report plateau common positive-superhump 0.09043(27) d. These values are stage/state dependent, not competing measurements of one invariant period.
why_it_matters: Superhump period and derived epsilon/q depend on stage; silently selecting or averaging periods distorts q and evolutionary diagnostics.
needed_action: Display early, late and modern plateau values with their event/stage; choose a canonical value only if the catalog defines a stage-specific convention.

competing_evidence: Urban & Sion+06 Table 2 fits Teff≈23000 K to a low-S/N composite IUE spectrum; WD accounts for 24% versus 76% disc FUV and paper says first estimates are approximate. No formal source-specific uncertainty.
why_it_matters: A precise WD Teff is often used for accretion-rate/cooling comparisons, but this fit is strongly composite/model dependent.
needed_action: Keep as approximate model output with explicit warning; for a precise Teff obtain a WD-dominated spectrum or reanalysis with component/continuum constraints.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 values 8.5±0.8e-12 (1–10 keV) and 1.5±0.2e-11 (0.1–10 keV) are approximate 4XMM-DR11 catalog conversions with >=10% errors; exact YZ XMM detection/epoch and absorption convention are not stated there. Hakala+04 separately gives direct 2002 XMM fit fluxes and a model bolometric flux.
why_it_matters: Fluxes may be interpreted as simultaneous with radio or directly comparable to source-specific spectral fits, affecting radio/X-ray ratios.
needed_action: Retain all values separately and request exact 4XMM-DR11 detection row/ID and conversion assumptions before deriving a source-specific luminosity or radio/X-ray ratio.

competing_evidence: A ~26 s optical oscillation is cited secondarily to Pezzuto+92 for one night; Hakala+04 did not recover it and warns short X-ray peaks are consistent with red noise. Original Pezzuto full text was not retrieved.
why_it_matters: Calling it WD spin would imply a secure rapid rotator and could alter classification/evolution interpretation.
needed_action: Do not list a confirmed WD spin unless original full text and an independent repeat establish coherence and physical origin.

competing_evidence: Gaia DR3 +21.9649/-55.1096 mas yr-1; HST FGS +17.5±0.9/-51.8±0.8; Coppejans+16 Table 1 gives +38±8/-58±8 from Skinner, Thorstensen & Lépine 2014. Gaia and HST agree more closely than the older compiled RA component.
why_it_matters: Proper motion affects epoch propagation and astrometric identity checks; disagreement could indicate old catalog/frame or reduction differences.
needed_action: Trace the 2014 compilation to its exact source and coordinate convention/epoch; retain Gaia as current astrometry unless a correction emerges.

competing_evidence: Dhillon+00 finds no donor spectral features and places a 20±5% K-band secondary contribution upper limit using M5V template; >=290 pc distance follows from donor sequence and surface-brightness assumptions. Sherrington & Jameson+83 K=14.365±0.08 is unresolved total system. This conflicts with Gaia 233 pc posterior.
why_it_matters: Misreading the M5V template/derived lower limit as a direct donor measurement or independent geometric distance would bias binary properties.
needed_action: Keep the >=290 pc result marked model dependent; do not adopt M5 or donor Teff without donor detection. If resolving distance conflict, re-evaluate template/scaling assumptions and K epoch/state.

competing_evidence: Dhillon+00 attributes an approximate ~130 pc prior distance to Patterson+84 based on H-beta/continuum discussion; Patterson+84 original full text was not retrieved during this audit.
why_it_matters: This is a large discrepancy if treated as a real geometric distance, but current claim is secondary-only and method may be obsolete.
needed_action: Retrieve and inspect the original Patterson+84 YZ Cnc entry/method before retaining a precise value; meanwhile label as secondary report only and exclude from preferred distance.

competing_evidence: Thorstensen, Wade & Oke+86 primary abstract gives 0.076351±0.000043 d; Coppejans+16 Appendix A1 uses 0.07637533(13) d as a refined phase ephemeris attributed to private communication.
why_it_matters: The precise ephemeris changes radio orbital phase, while the refined value is not a separately published analysis.
needed_action: For phase-sensitive comparisons, decide whether to use the private-communication ephemeris as a distinct adopted phase clock; retain both values and their provenance.

competing_evidence: Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior 220.14 pc (p16–p84 219.06–221.21) and photogeometric 220.22 pc; older estimates include 260 pc, Thorstensen+03 260(+190/−90) pc or alternate 403(+230/−162), and Urban & Sion+06 270 pc from weak parallax plus other priors.
why_it_matters: Distance choice shifts luminosity and absolute-magnitude comparisons; the legacy estimates combine heterogeneous priors.
needed_action: Use the Gaia geometric posterior for the compatibility field while retaining all literature branches; review if a population analysis requires a non-Gaia distance scale.

competing_evidence: Urban & Sion+06 low-S/N IUE WD+disc fit gives about 28,000 K with adopted Mwd=0.8 Msun and i=41°; its FUV shares are 55/45 and Mdot has order-of-magnitude uncertainty. Knigge+06 gives superhump-sequence estimates M2=0.105±0.023 Msun and R2=0.167±0.012 Rsun; nearby donor-sequence M5/~3100 K is not a SU UMa spectrum.
why_it_matters: Treating fit inputs, a low-S/N composite temperature, or a sequence node as direct component measurements would bias component/population comparisons.
needed_action: Keep model outputs and assumed inputs distinct in the machine-readable ledger; no direct donor type/temperature or dynamical masses are adopted. Confirm this is the preferred presentation for later catalog display.

competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 reports Benz+83 4.75-GHz outburst detection around 1.3 mJy and quiescent <0.4 mJy, but the 2.4-arcmin Effelsberg beam contains a nearby unclassified 33±9 μJy source 0.34 arcmin away. Benz+83 full table was not accessible; details are secondary-reported.
why_it_matters: The historical source association affects whether the system has a long-baseline radio history distinct from the 2015 VLA detections.
needed_action: Keep the 1983 claim flagged as secondary and potentially confused; retrieve the original full article or observing record before using its flux as a secure SU UMa measurement.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1–10 and 0.1–10 keV fluxes converted from Collins & Wheatley+10 MEKAL using PIMMS, average characteristic kT=11 keV and unabsorbed flux; no source-specific error, epoch/state or simultaneous radio match is supplied.
why_it_matters: These comparison-band fluxes are not native measurements at the radio epochs and can mislead radio/X-ray correlations if treated as simultaneous or directly fitted values.
needed_action: Keep fluxes labelled as model-dependent conversions and non-simultaneous; do not calculate a matched radio/X-ray ratio without an explicit state/epoch model.

competing_evidence: O’Donoghue+03 proposes weak transfer/hibernating-CV interpretation; Matranga+12 detects narrow X-ray eclipses and fits (1.694±0.046)×10^-13 M_sun/yr in 2006; Parsons+11/+16 favor detached/pre-CV with donor at 96–97% Roche fill; Drake+14 estimates ~10^-16 M_sun/yr from 1999 HST photospheric metals and diffusion.
why_it_matters: Materially affects whether QS Vir is labeled detached/pre-CV, hibernating CV, or low-rate accretor and whether radio emission is connected to mass transfer.
needed_action: Keep class/state values epoch- and method-specific. Please decide whether the community catalog should use a broad PCEB/pre-CV primary label with CV-accretion evidence as a secondary flag, or another explicit scheme; do not merge the published accretion rates.

competing_evidence: Parsons+16 infers ~100 kG (~0.1 MG) weak WD field from Mg II 4481 Å line broadening and favors that over rapid rotation; the same broadening if rotational implies Pspin~700 s. Parsons+11 says Mg II indicates the WD is not rapidly rotating; Matranga+12 places a conservative B<1 MG limit from Balmer core widths/no Zeeman or cyclotron features.
why_it_matters: Confusing a tentative photospheric field, a conditional spin estimate, or an upper limit with a direct field/spin measurement would bias the magnetic-CV versus weak-field comparison.
needed_action: Do not adopt a measured spin or field. If a preferred display value is required, decide whether to show ~0.1 MG as tentative inference alongside <1 MG limit or leave only the upper limit. Spectropolarimetry around Mg II is needed to discriminate.

competing_evidence: Qian+10 proposed a ~7.86 yr circumbinary planet; Parsons+10b found a large ~250 s timing deviation, rejected Qian’s solution, and fit an approximate ~14 yr eccentric body; Horner+13 found proposed configurations dynamically unstable (<1000 yr); Pulley+25 reports new minima invalidate the recent models and publishes a quadratic ephemeris with coefficient −8.6(6)×10^-13 d cycle^-2.
why_it_matters: A fitted quadratic term, a physical Pdot, and a circumbinary companion are different claims; conflation creates a false evolutionary/planetary inference.
needed_action: Retain the ephemeris coefficient as an empirical fit only; do not publish a physical Pdot or companion without a justified model and updated timing analysis. Confirm any future interpretation against new eclipse timings.

competing_evidence: Ridder+25 §2.1 states VLA observations on 2022-11-28, 2022-12-28, 2023-01-09, while Tables 2–4 label the middle epoch 2022-12-22. Corrigendum corrects spectral-index signs but does not address this mismatch.
why_it_matters: The date sets radio observation state/phase and the relationship to Swift observations on 2022-12-31.
needed_action: Check the VLA project archive (22B-257) or authors’ data/products to establish the middle epoch’s true date; until then retain the table’s 2022-12-22 label and flag the prose conflict.

competing_evidence: Rawdog inherited 8.5±0.9×10^-13 erg cm^-2 s^-1 at 1–10 keV with Webb+20 as sole citation. Ridder+23 Table 4 is the source of the converted comparison flux; §3.2 says 4XMM-DR11 full-band minus Bands 1–2 and that errors are floored at 10%. The value is not a source-specific spectral fit or contemporaneous with radio.
why_it_matters: Mislabeling a catalogue-based approximate conversion as a direct XMM spectral measurement or simultaneous radio/X-ray datum can bias radio/X-ray luminosity comparisons.
needed_action: Keep Webb+20 as catalogue paper and Ridder+23 as conversion/source table; preserve the 10% error floor, band convention, and epoch/state limitation. Do not calculate a simultaneous radio/X-ray ratio from it.

competing_evidence: Ridder+25 cites older radio-flare and upper-limit claims from the 1980s; original observation papers/tables and exact epoch/frequency details were not retrieved in this audit.
why_it_matters: Historical values may alter the radio variability baseline and would be unsafe to blend with modern VLA epochs without original methods and state information.
needed_action: Retrieve and inspect the original Dulk/Bastian/Chanmugam papers and any follow-up limits; add values only with exact observing frequency, epoch, flux convention and original-table citation.

competing_evidence: Stark+08 calls 1RXS J165630.2-083442 the likely optical counterpart; exact RASS-BSC separation ~9.7 arcsec with 10 arcsec position error. 2RXS is ~8.2 arcsec from Gaia. Pointed 1WGA is ~16.7 arcsec away with a 90% 50-arcsec radius; SIMBAD does not list the WGA alias.
why_it_matters: Association affects X-ray luminosity and radio/X-ray comparison.
needed_action: Retain as probable; confirm with higher-resolution X-ray data/archive astrometry before calling the ROSAT flux securely matched.

competing_evidence: Stark+08 reports 0.1952894(10) d. Bruch & Diaz+17 reports refined 0.1952913(3) d from 2015 line-phase offsets and baseline-scaled uncertainty. Hewitt+20 repeats Stark. The two measurements differ by 1.9e-6 d (~1.8 sigma from quoted errors).
why_it_matters: The period sets long-term phase predictions and errors are method dependent.
needed_action: For phase-sensitive use, review retaining Bruch & Diaz as compatibility value; keep both values and uncertainty methods.

competing_evidence: Stark+08 DIB 5780 gives E(B−V)~0.50 if narrow component alone or ~0.24 for narrow+broad (authors prefer latter); DIB 4430 gives ~0.12. Schlegel full-column is ~0.47 and not source-specific. IX Vel color comparison suggests ~0.10; authors deem 0.10–0.20 plausible.
why_it_matters: Extinction shifts CMD color and absolute magnitude; arbitrary selection would bias intrinsic comparisons.
needed_action: Keep observed Gaia CMD values. If intrinsic CMD needed, determine source-specific reddening from updated 3D dust or spectroscopy; preserve published branches.

competing_evidence: Bruch & Diaz+17 arbitrary overlay uses i=60°, M2=.43 Msun, q=.52 from M1=.83 in prose, but Fig. 5 caption says M1=.75. Hewitt+20 SED inputs M1=.75, M2=.45 Msun, i=57°, Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr are explicitly unknown/estimated. None are source-specific measurements.
references: Bruch+Diaz+17_LSIV-08-3; Hewitt+20; Knigge+11 as cited by Bruch
why_it_matters: Mislabeling assumptions as measurements would bias component comparisons.
needed_action: Keep out of measured-value fields. Decide only whether future public display needs a separate model-assumptions section.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 reports <33 uJy; §4.2 notes and rejects a roughly 3-sigma feature about 6 arcsec from optical position.
why_it_matters: Treating the feature as detection changes the radio status and population comparison.
needed_action: Retain upper limit; verify astrometry from raw images if available before representing as a candidate.

competing_evidence: SIMBAD object type is CV*, but its sp_type field says sdB. Stark+08 documents earlier OB/hot-subdwarf classification and reclassifies as UX UMa CV; the SIMBAD label appears legacy rather than a component spectrum.
why_it_matters: Using stale sdB metadata as a WD/donor type would misidentify physical components.
needed_action: Retain as historical/conflicting metadata only; any public type must include source/date and not assign sdB to a component.

competing_evidence: Frew (2008, Appendix B.2) favors ambient low-excitation H II gas photoionized by disk/WD and a wind bow shock; Bond & Miszalski (2018, §6) allow chance ISM-cloud encounter or old nova ejecta; Castro Segura et al. (2021, §§3.6.1, 4.1) suggest a possible ~900-1000 yr shell from proper-motion back-projection; Iłkiewicz et al. (2026, §3.2, Fig. 3) report layered W2/H-alpha morphology, favor wind/ISM structure, but explicitly cannot exclude a shell.
why_it_matters: A shell identification affects nova recurrence and evolutionary comparisons; current evidence does not establish one origin.
needed_action: Keep origin unresolved. Future expansion/kinematic and abundance measurements, especially nitrogen, are needed to distinguish ejecta from ambient gas/wind cavity.

competing_evidence: Bond & Miszalski (2018) report 0.15216 +/-0.00002 d = 3.65184 +/-0.00048 h from 2006 H-alpha RVs. Castro Segura et al. (2021) combine 2006, 2017 and 2018 RVs across ~27000 cycles and report 0.15220606(6) d = 3.6529454 +0.0000016/-0.0000013 h. The ~3.98 s difference is ~2.3 times the older formal error; Castro Segura say separate-season estimates agree within errors.
why_it_matters: The orbital clock controls phase, velocity-derived q, and period-dependent population comparisons.
needed_action: Retain both values and provisionally use the long-baseline combined ephemeris. Reconcile per-season velocities, aliases, epoch convention and covariance before calling the old value discrepant or superseded.

competing_evidence: Castro Segura et al. (2021) report q=M2/M1=0.51 +/-0.03(stat) +0.4/-0.2(sys), depending on donor irradiation correction and disk-shadow geometry. An expected sequence donor M2≈0.26 Msun gives M1≈0.5 Msun (≈0.55 Msun with no shadowing); authors say the low result suggests K velocities may be proxies and needs confirmation. Hewitt et al. (2020) Table 4 assumes M1=0.75 and M2=0.27 Msun for SED.
why_it_matters: Treating a sequence/model inference as a WD mass measurement would bias WD-mass and evolutionary comparisons.
needed_action: Keep q with separate statistical/systematic errors and leave the wide-table WD mass blank pending independent donor absorption or dynamical constraints.

competing_evidence: Native 2SXPS row 187732 gives 0.3-10 keV observed flux 1.309e-12 and power-law-unabsorbed flux 1.58e-12 erg cm-2 s-1. Ridder et al. (2023) convert to 1-10 keV 1.2 +/-0.2e-12 and 0.1-10 keV 1.5 +/-0.3e-12, but Table 4 does not mark absorbed/unabsorbed. Castro Segura et al. (2021) separately fit two Swift epochs with a low-count two-component model.
why_it_matters: Absorption and spectral model affect comparison of X-ray output across CVs, WD pulsars and transients.
needed_action: Keep native observed/unabsorbed 2SXPS and Ridder comparison fluxes separate. Verify exact model/conversion inputs and absorbed convention before selecting one comparison flux.

competing_evidence: Frew (2008) derives nebular E(B-V)=0.04 +/-0.04 from Fr 2-11's Balmer decrement and reports total-to-infinity map E(B-V)=0.144. Neither is a binary-specific Gaia correction; Gaia photometry is unresolved variable accretion-system light. M_G is retained without extinction and BP-RP is observed.
why_it_matters: Reddening choices change intrinsic CMD color and extinction-corrected M_G and may not describe the unresolved binary.
needed_action: Leave intrinsic color and extinction-corrected M_G blank until an applicable source-specific reddening and extinction law are justified; record whether nebular decrement is applicable to the binary.

competing_evidence: Frew (2008) Appendix B.2.1 prose reports log F(H-beta)=-11.4 erg cm-2 s-1, corresponding to 3.98e-12 erg cm-2 s-1. Table B.1 footnote on the same printed page reports F(H-beta)=1.05e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 with c(H-beta)=0.06. These differ by about 379x. The prose value gives H-alpha/H-beta≈2.8 using the prose log F(H-alpha)=-10.95, consistent with the stated intrinsic Balmer ratio; the footnote value does not. Both original-text claims are visually checked; neither is silently preferred.
why_it_matters: The Balmer decrement supports the cited E(B-V) and nebular interpretation. Choosing the wrong integrated flux would misstate nebular brightness and potentially undermine reddening provenance.
needed_action: Keep both claims separately ledgered. Verify against the thesis source image/original reduced SHASSA measurement or a Frew erratum/author clarification; determine whether Table B.1 value has a transcription, exponent, or aperture-definition issue before adopting a single integrated flux.

competing_evidence: Hartley+05 gives i>65 deg as a pure estimate; Ribeiro & Diaz+07 formal interval 45–75; Linnell+09 adopts 65±2 and fits the SED; Hewitt+20 uses 60 deg as model input; Gilmozzi & Selvelli+24 adopt 60±15 after reporting Bruch ~65, la Dous <50 and Puebla ~30–50 from prior literature. Some underlying original values are only secondarily checked.
why_it_matters: Inclination corrections affect disk luminosity and accretion-rate estimates; choosing one branch may change population comparisons.
needed_action: Keep each model/literature branch separate; do not publish one canonical inclination. For a single-value analysis, choose a method-specific branch and inspect the original sources and eclipse evidence.

competing_evidence: 2SXPS row 175084 gives 0.3–10 keV power-law observed 3.821e-12 and unabsorbed 5.22e-12 erg cm-2 s-1. Ridder+23 gives 4.8±0.5e-12 (1–10 keV) and 6.1±0.6e-12 (0.1–10 keV), with 10% error floor and 7-keV MEKAL assumption for novalikes lacking source fit; absorbed convention/epoch is unspecified.
why_it_matters: Band, absorption convention and assumed spectrum change X-ray luminosity and radio/X-ray comparisons; values are not known simultaneous.
needed_action: Keep native 2SXPS observed/unabsorbed products and Ridder comparison bands separate. Choose a preferred value only after checking source-specific spectrum/NH and observation epoch.

competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 configures 856 MHz bandwidth centered 1.284 GHz (0.856–1.712 GHz); Ridder+23 labels the same 256±26 μJy point as 0.43–2.1 GHz. Compatibility band uses the primary setup and retains Ridder label in the ledger.
why_it_matters: Incorrect passband metadata can distort spectral-energy and population comparisons.
needed_action: Confirm whether Ridder band is a generic label or compilation error; use Hewitt exact setup for frequency-sensitive analysis meanwhile.

competing_evidence: SIMBAD sp_type=sdB cites Bond & Landolt (1971). Its title/abstract describe a peculiar subluminous B-type star and possible WD relation; only abstract metadata checked. Cowley et al. (1977) full article identifies the close accreting binary, later classified as nova-like CV.
why_it_matters: Using a legacy preliminary spectrum as a WD atmospheric or donor subtype would misidentify binary components.
needed_action: Keep sdB only as historical metadata. Retrieve and inspect the full 1971 article if a definitive explanation/correction is needed.
public_status: Awaiting access to the original source

competing_evidence: Gilmozzi & Selvelli+24 independently derive E(B−V)=0.02±0.02 using the IUE 2175 Å feature. Linnell+09 adopts 0.02 from Bruch & Engel+94 catalog (no error) and cites Verbunt+87 preferred 0 with <0.04 upper bound; Mauche+88 reports the bound secondarily. Original Verbunt/Bruch & Engel source rows were not checked.
why_it_matters: Reddening affects intrinsic color/M_G; current Gaia CMD remains observed unresolved-system values without extinction correction.
needed_action: Keep branches separate; do not publish intrinsic BP−RP or extinction-corrected M_G until original source chain and appropriate Gaia-band correction are verified.

competing_evidence: Tappert+04 Table 7: P3=0.062887(37)d (pd=.637 most probable) and P4=0.060972(14)d (pd=.272 important); five aliases total and more observations needed. Hewitt+20 repeats P3 as Porb.
why_it_matters: A canonical orbit affects period distributions, donor sequence and evolutionary comparisons.
needed_action: Keep P3 as a candidate only; use follow-up photometry/spectroscopy to confirm before promoting to secure orbital period.

competing_evidence: Tappert calls spectrum DN-like with strong H-alpha; Hewitt includes source in novalike sample but allows missed-outburst DN.
why_it_matters: Subtype labels determine population grouping.
needed_action: Retain provisional DN-like CV/novalike-sample membership with subtype unresolved unless light-curve/outburst evidence warrants a final label.

competing_evidence: 2RXS row links to 1RXS at 0.7 arcsec, SIMBAD links 1RXS to V5662/Gaia, but 2RXS centroid is ~19.2 arcsec from Gaia propagated J2000 and has only 18.71+/-5.11 counts.
why_it_matters: The counterpart decides whether ROSAT properties belong to this CV.
needed_action: Inspect 2RXS images/localization or ROSAT event products and decide whether to accept the catalog link; keep flux qualified pending review.

competing_evidence: Ridder Table 4 has 3.3+/-0.9e-12 (1-10 keV) and 4.2+/-1.1e-12 (0.1-10 keV); §3.2 describes MEKAL 7-keV/PIMMS-type conversion, but source-specific input and absorbed/unabsorbed convention are unstated. Boller flux is separate absorption-corrected ROSAT fit with poorly constrained Gamma.
why_it_matters: Luminosity comparisons depend on band, assumed spectrum and absorption, and correct counterpart.
needed_action: Recover source-specific conversion inputs if available; otherwise retain separately with unspecified convention and do not calculate preferred Lx.

competing_evidence: Hewitt says optical sampling is too poor to determine if V5662 was in low state near 2019-04-01 MeerKAT epoch.
why_it_matters: Radio emission may depend on accretion state; an incorrect state assignment biases comparison.
needed_action: Keep state unknown unless contemporaneous observations establish it.

competing_evidence: HST/FGS solutions span 6.02±0.46 mas (Harrison+99), 6.06±0.44 (Harrison+04), 8.30±0.41 (Nelan & Bond 2013), and 7.3±0.2 mas in the Harrison & McArthur 2016 AAS abstract; Harrison+16 footnote gives 7.41±0.20 mas. Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior is 112.35 pc and VLBI is 114±2 pc.
why_it_matters: Distance changes luminosities and distance-dependent accretion/WD-atmosphere interpretations; the HST re-reductions are not mutually consistent.
needed_action: Keep every astrometric solution separate and use Gaia geometric posterior only for the compatibility distance. If one historical solution is needed, retrieve/compare the 2016 HST/FGS reduction products or obtain clarification from its authors; do not average.

competing_evidence: Sion+10 gives 46 kK at E(B−V)=0.04 and 55 kK at 0.07 with 166 pc; Sion & Godon+15 refits at 114–120 pc and gives 45–50 kK, representative 47 kK, with fixed assumed 0.95 Msun.
why_it_matters: WD heating/accretion comparisons depend on reddening, distance, mass and fit assumptions; averaging would hide model branches.
needed_action: For a future canonical summary, decide whether to display the updated-distance refit as the preferred model branch while retaining older reddening branches, or show all branches without a single preferred range. No new atmosphere refit is performed here.

competing_evidence: Accretion-state-dependent DNOs vary 7.81→6.59→2.91→2.85 s in 1996 (Mauche & Robinson 2001); XRISM line width implies 16–44 s only if rotational, while no 10–50 s timing signal was detected (Ishida+26); Sharp+26 reports optical QPO-like peaks 0.25–8 h.
why_it_matters: Conflating these clocks would produce a false WD spin distribution and could bias comparisons with WD pulsars or LPTs.
needed_action: Keep numeric wd_spin_period_s blank. Decide later whether a distinct model-inferred spin-candidate field should expose 16–44 s; keep DNOs and optical QPOs in their own component-qualified fields unless independent coherent spin periodicity is detected.

competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 gives 9.0±0.9×10−10 and 4.1(+0.5/−0.4)×10−11 erg cm−2 s−1 in nominal unabsorbed 1–10 keV, based on Swift spectra; the two points are maxima in different bands and their SS Cyg observation IDs/model/NH/conversion are not printed.
why_it_matters: Flux comparison and luminosity interpretation depend on band conversion, absorption convention and epoch; values are not proven simultaneous with radio.
needed_action: If exact Swift extraction must be reproduced, identify ObsIDs and fitted model/NH or PIMMS settings in the UK Swift archive/Ridder materials. Retain both published estimates with this limitation until then.

competing_evidence: Bitner+07 assigns K4.5 V±0.5 and 4470±140 K from a spectral-type scale with systematics; Harrison+16 IJHK synthetic spectrum gives 4750 K, subsolar Fe/C/Mg, and discusses apparent K3.5 versus inclination-corrected K2.5.
why_it_matters: Roche distortion, inclination, irradiation/spots and metallicity affect spectral appearance; a donor Teff should not be interpreted as a unique single-star temperature.
needed_action: For future online summaries, keep the calibrated subtype/temperature and IJHK atmosphere result as distinct method-tagged measurements; choose a canonical display only if a use case requires one.

competing_evidence: Abstract states a 43-MG synchrotron-region field; §4.1 and Table 2 give about 43 G (Table 2: 42.7±0.2 G fast cooling, 20 G slow cooling) and then separately infer a ~15-MG WD polar field at a modeled location. The abstract/body difference is a factor of 10^6. References: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco; Garnavich+21_ARSco.
why_it_matters: This changes the inferred local field by six orders of magnitude and the extrapolated WD field by two orders; field location and model are not interchangeable.
needed_action: Check for a publisher correction or request author clarification of the abstract unit and the Table 2/body model units. Until then, retain the table/body G result and the abstract MG claim as distinct unresolved entries; do not select a global WD field.

competing_evidence: The 2025 abstract gives Pspin=117.0564 s and a 58.26-s modulation. Its §3.2 gives the periodogram peak 17.053(23) mHz =58.641(79) s and compares it with twice Pelisoli+22 nu_spin=17.0764365689(59) mHz; the 2025 full text elsewhere uses 117.12 s. References: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco; Pelisoli+22_ARSco.
why_it_matters: An incorrect period could conflate a spin fundamental, a harmonic and the beat; the accepted timing solution makes the 220-GHz peak a near-2-spin harmonic, not a new 58-s spin.
needed_action: Verify abstract numbers against the journal record/corrigendum/authors. Preserve the body periodogram value and published Pelisoli spin/beat clocks separately meanwhile.

competing_evidence: Barrett & Gurwell §3.1 reports mean S220=124±2 mJy, with range 77–167 mJy; Appendix B Table 3 gives 124±10 mJy for SMA 220 GHz. Reference: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco.
why_it_matters: Flux uncertainty affects spectral-index and SED model constraints, including the inferred field.
needed_action: Check the paper table/text or any erratum/source data to identify statistical versus calibration uncertainty; keep both published entries until resolved.

parameter: mass ratio, WD mass and inclination model
competing_evidence: Marsh+16 defines q=M2/M1 and q>0.35, with WD allowed mass 0.81–1.29 M_sun. du Plessis+19 uses q=M1/M2 and reports q=3.45(+0.66/-0.45) and MWD=1.00(+0.16/-0.10) M_sun assuming i≈zeta and Roche-lobe filling. du Plessis+22 later finds RVM alpha/zeta fits vary by ~10/~30 degrees over orbital phase. References: Marsh+16; duPlessis+19_ARSco; duPlessis+22_ARSco.
why_it_matters: Mixing inverse q conventions or promoting zeta to orbital i can change mass conclusions and propagate into evolutionary comparisons.
needed_action: Retain the published solutions with explicit conventions and model assumptions. Decide whether the 2019 model mass remains suitable for a preferred catalog field after considering phase-resolved fit behavior; no single mass is selected in the ledger.

competing_evidence: Field claims refer to different components/methods: Garnavich+21 photospheric Ly-alpha upper limit <=100 MG; Buckley+17 <=500 MG vacuum-dipole spin-down upper scale; Katz+17 abstract ~100 MG but Table 1 Bp=1.1e9–3.6e9*csc(theta) G and mu=4.3e34–1.5e35*csc(theta) G cm3 for mass alternatives; Lyutikov+20 ~1 MG propeller model; Barrett+25 body/Table local ~43-G field and modeled ~15-MG pole if corrected as printed. References listed.
why_it_matters: A single catalogued field or moment would conflate a photospheric upper limit, polar field, local emission-region model and theoretical torque estimates.
needed_action: No single WD field or moment is designated as measured. Verify the Barrett unit issue; retain all other model branches with geometry/mass/torque assumptions, and confirm any use of a preferred field/moment in downstream science.

competing_evidence: Marsh+16 report no clear accretion-disc/broad-line evidence and spin-down-powered energetics; Pelisoli+22 finds the donor close to Roche-lobe filling; Lyutikov+20 proposes a transient low-field propeller with mass loading; Barrett+25 argues for a temporarily ceased accretion/IP-like phase; Buckley+26 describes detached or nearly detached WDP binaries.
why_it_matters: The state classification affects whether a binary-evolution connection is claimed; none of these observations establishes one unique evolutionary path.
needed_action: Keep WDP as the observed class. For a database-level detached/semi-detached flag, decide whether to leave it unresolved pending the forthcoming 2020 multiwavelength primary papers; do not promote a proposed IP/polar/LPT evolutionary pathway.

competing_evidence: Buckley+26 conference proceedings report coherent NICER spin pulsations, L-band MeerKAT variable/polarized emission closer to spin modulation, and a recent rotational Fermi-LAT signal. The review says the June 2020 campaign results will appear in forthcoming papers and gives no fluxes, period uncertainties, energy bands or calibration. Earlier Singh+20 Fermi analysis is summarized as only a 2-sigma upper limit. References: Buckley+26_ARSco; duPlessis+22_ARSco.
why_it_matters: New high-energy/radio pulses would add an independent emission component and may alter mechanism interpretation; secondary summaries are insufficient for adoption.
needed_action: Locate and inspect the promised primary NICER/MeerKAT/Fermi papers or data release; until verified, record only the proceedings report and do not mark gamma-ray detection confirmed.

competing_evidence: The physical table inherited ~8e34 G cm3 attributed to Buckley+17. The checked Buckley text reports a 500-MG spin-down upper field but no direct magnetic-moment value; Katz+17 Table 1 explicitly gives 4.3e34–1.5e35*csc(theta) G cm3 under vacuum-dipole assumptions. References: Buckley+17_ARSco; Katz+17_ARSco.
why_it_matters: The legacy scalar lacks a traceable formula/radius convention and may be mistaken for a measured moment.
needed_action: Keep the unsupported 8e34 claim out of the preferred moment field; retain Katz’s explicit mass/angle-dependent model range and record no measured moment.

competing_evidence: Discovery Pelisoli+23 reports M1=1.2 +/- 0.2 Msun and an inclination ceiling below 37 deg from optical/Roche assumptions, including H-beta/L1 geometry. HST/COS Pelisoli+23_J1912UV fits give adopted M1=0.59 +/- 0.05 Msun; updated UV metal-line/Roche analysis gives i=59 +/- 6 deg, and q constraints change. The UV paper says the former mass is about 3 sigma above its fit.
why_it_matters: Changes component masses, binary geometry, and any population/evolutionary comparison; the two results use different tracers and model assumptions.
needed_action: Choose whether the public wide table should expose the later UV atmosphere/model mass as provisional or leave a scalar blank/unresolved. Preserve both values and methods in the ledger; verify the dynamical line-tracer/Roche correction before adopting a single mass.

competing_evidence: Pelisoli+23_J1912UV Table 2 prints individual radii 0.0131, 0.0119, 0.0138 Rsun (each +/-0.004) but the adopted row prints 0.128 +/- 0.040 Rsun. The accepted manuscript PDF table was visually checked; the discrepancy is present in the printed table.
why_it_matters: The adopted value is physically inconsistent with the individual fits/mass scale by about a factor of ten; blindly correcting it would invent an unpublished correction.
